body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: a827ec626cab7298d2cc9ad616258dd050146c2b -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

**What looks good**
- Input audit: `WireContourOp` (crates/app/src/operation/types/wire_edm.rs:27-53) has seven stored words: `top_z`, `bottom_z`, `condition`, `side`, `start`, `burnout`, `clearance`. The Wire Contour stamp arm (crates/app/src/operation/params.rs:1441-1478 after the change) now digests all seven. The wire diameter and gap come in through `wire_op::stamp_condition`. The stamp has no missing input.
- Die and Punch still write `0` and `1`, so no closed cut goes Stale on upgrade. Left and Right write `2` and `3`, then the clearance. An open run saved before this change reads Stale once and clears on regenerate. That is the right direction for a safety stamp.
- Layering is clean: the change is one stamp arm plus one new test file, with no schema or command changes. `wire_stamp.rs` is 219 lines and carries a provenance header.

**Local results** (PR head trial-merged with current `upstream/main`, which carries #1367, #1372 and #1147; merged clean)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `wire_stamp` | 3 passed |
| `wire_contour` | 8 passed |
| `wire_burnout` | 3 passed |
| `wire_post` | 8 passed |
| `wire_readers` | 7 passed |
| `wire_verify` | 3 passed |
| `mcp_wire_contour` | 4 passed |
| `edm_conditions` | 2 passed |
| `feature_pick_wire` | 4 passed, 1 ignored |
| `project_roundtrip` | 73 passed |
| `operations` | 119 passed, 6 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

I did not run the pixel snapshots, the GUI, or the ui crate. The PR touches neither.

**Mutation check of the pins** (each mutation applied to `params.rs`, `wire_stamp` rerun, source restored; the PR diff is unchanged afterwards)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Left byte 2 changed to 3 (Left collides with Right) | 2 of 3 fail |
| Left's clearance dropped | `the_four_sides_stamp_apart...` fails; the file test passes |
| Right's clearance dropped | 2 of 3 fail |
| Right byte 3 changed to 2 (Right collides with Left) | 2 of 3 fail |
| Clearance also written for Die (closed cut would churn) | `the_four_sides_stamp_apart...` fails |

Every new stamp field and discriminant is caught by at least one pin. The closed-cut non-regression, where Die and Punch ignore the clearance, is pinned too.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. Dropping Left's clearance is caught only by the four-sides test, not by the file-door test. That test restates the clearance on one open side only, so the file test alone would pass. It is still pinned, so no change is required. Restating it on both sides would make the file test cover both.
2. The PR notes that #1163, #1181 and #1218 touch the same arm. Whichever merges second needs a hand-merge that keeps `taper_deg` and these side bytes.
3. No `docs/decisions` file. The `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1370` and the conventional subject are all present.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
